text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller urges opposition and media not to make provocative statements about possible military intervention against the Islamist-led government.
- Parliament to pass law banning use of mobile telephones while driving.
- Opposition parties in talks to topple government and set up secularist left-right coalition.
- Government prepares to give civil servants wage rises in January of up to eight percentage points above inflation.
- Ciller threatens to sack Interior Minister Mehmet Agar for criticising Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's visit to Libya.
- European Union may be prepared to lift embargo on breakaway north Cyprus state.
- Volume of foreign investment in Istanbul stock exchange rose by 17.3 percent last month.
- Backbenchers in conservative True Path Party close to rebellion against Ciller's leadership.
- Teachers still want to take up posts in the southeast despite Kurdish rebel attacks on teachers there.
